g1.label: 1. The event director chooses the venue alone: “Book it today.”
g1.why: The director decides alone and gives an instruction: autocratic.

g2.label: 2. The manager asks everyone’s view and the team decides together.
g2.why: The team is involved in the decision: democratic (participative).

g3.label: 3. “You know this better than I do. Decide, and tell me afterwards.”
g3.why: The manager hands the decision to the experts: laissez-faire (delegative).

g4.label: 4. A bonus for 200 tickets; no place next year if you miss it.
g4.why: Targets, rewards and consequences are the transactional style.

g5.label: 5. The greenest festival in Europe; each person takes on a new challenge.
g5.why: A vision that inspires people to grow is transformational.

g6.label: 6. The manager does the admin and asks: “How can I help?”
g6.why: Putting the team’s needs first and removing obstacles is servant leadership.

g7.correct: adapt their style to the situation
accept: adapt their style to the situation
g7.label: 7. According to the text, most good managers ___.
g7.why: The last paragraph says they adapt to the situation, the task and the people.

g1.label: 1. Nobody likes a boss who checks every email. She tends to ___ her team.
g1.why: To micromanage is to control every small detail of other people’s work.

g2.label: 2. She knows when to ___ tasks to others.
g2.why: To delegate a task to someone is to give it to them to do.

g3.label: 3. If the team doesn’t agree with the plan, you won’t get their ___.
g3.why: Buy-in is people’s agreement and support for a plan.

g4.label: 4. Our manager gives us a lot of ___: we choose how and when we work.
g4.why: Autonomy is the freedom to decide for yourself.

g5.label: 5. In a ___ organisation, decisions are made by senior management and passed down.
g5.why: Top-down: decisions come from the top and go down to staff.

g6.label: 6. She is very ___: she helps set up the stalls herself.
g6.why: A hands-on manager is personally involved in the work.

g7.label: 7. Good training and trust ___ staff to solve problems without permission.
g7.why: To empower someone is to give them the confidence and authority to act.

g8.label: 8. Before he changes the budget, the director will ___ the finance team.
g8.why: To consult people is to ask for their views before deciding.

g9.label: 9. If something goes wrong, there is clear ___: everyone knows who is responsible.
g9.why: Accountability means being responsible for results and able to explain them.

g10.label: 10. The CEO can ___ a decision made by the team.
g10.why: To overrule a decision is to cancel it using higher authority.

g1.label: 1. An autocratic manager usually makes a ___ decision.
g1.why: The autocratic manager decides alone, so the decision comes from the top.

g2.label: 2. Asks for everyone’s views, then decides alone: the manager is being ___.
g2.why: Listening first and then deciding alone is a consultative decision.

g3.label: 3. Keeps talking until every person agrees: the team is aiming for ___.

g4.label: 4. A laissez-faire manager often ___ the decision to the people who do the work.
g4.why: Laissez-faire managers give decisions to the team: they delegate.
